Current labeling states the output is a quantitative score for clinician interpretation and explicitly does not diagnose coronary artery disease. cases.device_description: A locked AI device cleared through 510(k) with no authorized predetermined change control plan. The manufacturer maintains an internal product roadmap that lists 'quarterly model refresh with the same architecture, same input, same output, and acceptance criteria of non-inferiority on a 500-case holdout'. The proposed refresh satisfies every element of that roadmap, and the holdout run shows no regression on the primary metric and no subgroup degradation. The manufacturer argues that the roadmap is functionally a PCCP because it pre-specifies changes, methodology, and acceptance criteria, and that the refresh therefore does not require a new submission.

cases.device_description: A chest radiograph triage model whose PCCP acceptance criteria require the primary metric plus subgroup floors for three predefined subgroups and reporting of confidence intervals. This cycle reports the primary metric with 95 percent confidence intervals, and the subgroup table shows results for two of the three subgroups; the third subgroup had fewer than the protocol's minimum of 40 cases, so it was omitted rather than reported as underpowered. The manufacturer argues that omitting an underpowered subgroup is more honest than reporting an unreliable estimate, and that the change otherwise meets all gates.

cases.device_description: A device whose PCCP acceptance criterion is stated as a lower bound of the 95 percent confidence interval for sensitivity of at least 0.90 on the holdout. This cycle reports point sensitivity of 0.928 on 260 cases, with a 95 percent CI of 0.891 to 0.955. The manufacturer argues that the point estimate clears the bar and that the interval's lower bound misses only because the holdout is small; a supplemental read on 120 additional cases is planned next quarter.
